clue.text: Will settlement

definitions.meaning: will as in strength of purpose, resolve
the settling or deciding of a dispute or question

explanation.definitionFit: Both resolve of purpose and the final deciding of a matter are senses of the same noun.

clue.text: Authorised new poem about soldier getting married

indicators.note: new signals that the letters of poem are made into a fresh arrangement
about means the word for married goes round the soldier

parts.note: married means wed
RE, the Royal Engineers, stands for a soldier or sapper

explanation.surface: A soldier's wedding is marked by a newly authorised poem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Authorised' is the definition; RE is the usual crossword soldier, from the Royal Engineers.
explanation.definitionFit: To be given authority or power to act is to be authorised.

clue.text: That is up to the German flier

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: der is a German word for the

explanation.surface: Someone says it is now the German's turn.
explanation.definitionFit: The eider is a sea duck, a bird and so a flier.

clue.text: Crazed fellow in charge

parts.note: a fellow is a man

explanation.surface: A deranged man is running the show.
explanation.definitionFit: Manic and crazed are synonyms for wildly frenzied behaviour.

clue.text: King Rat featuring in simple story

indicators.note: featuring in means appearing inside the simple word

parts.note: simple means naive
R, for Rex, is king
taken as written

explanation.surface: A rat with a crown appears in a children's tale.
explanation.definitionFit: A narrative is an account of events, a story.

clue.text: Unspoiled Hardy heroine is not a novice at heart

indicators.note: at heart means the next pieces sit in the middle of the heroine's name

parts.note: Tess of the d'Urbervilles is Thomas Hardy's heroine
ain't is a colloquial form of is not
L, a learner, is a novice

explanation.surface: Hardy's heroine is unspoiled, though experienced at heart.
explanation.walkthrough: L is the learner plate on a British car, hence a novice.
explanation.definitionFit: Something without a taint or blemish is unspoiled.

clue.text: Poem about church ladies performed in concert hall

parts.note: an ode is a poem

indicators.note: about means the letters for church ladies are turned round

parts.note: MU is the Mothers' Union, a Church of England women's organisation

explanation.surface: Church women recite a poem in a concert hall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns MU into UM. 'performed in' links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An odeum is a building for musical performances, a concert hall in ancient Greece or Rome.

clue.text: Going round and right to stop going round on the cricket pitch

parts.note: something bowling along is rolling round

indicators.note: going round means the word for stop surrounds the letter for right

parts.note: to stop is to cease

explanation.surface: Something spinning is stopped by a right turn, all on a cricket pitch.
explanation.walkthrough: The second 'going round' puts R inside CEASE.
explanation.definitionFit: The bowling crease is the white line marked on a cricket pitch from which the bowler delivers.

clue.text: Flag America's put up, for example, as usual

parts.note: a standard is a flag
USA is America

indicators.note: in a down clue, put up means the letters read upwards

explanation.surface: An American flag is raised in the customary way.
explanation.definitionFit: Standard usage is the customary way of doing or saying things, what is usual.

clue.text: Urban work by sanctimonious boy

parts.note: op., opus, is a work
pi is slang for sanctimonious, pious
Dan is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A goody-goody boy produces some city-themed work.
explanation.definitionFit: Oppidan, from Latin oppidum, a town, means of a town, urban.

clue.text: One with soldiers in desert clothing

indicators.note: in means the one and the soldiers go inside the word for desert

parts.note: to rat is to desert
I is the Roman numeral one
soldiers are men

explanation.surface: A lone figure and some troops in a desert wearing robes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'desert' is a verb, not the sandy place.
explanation.definitionFit: Raiment is an old word for clothing.

clue.text: Under a cow?

definitions.meaning: a cow lows, so whimsically it is one that lows

explanation.definitionFit: Lower means further down or under; a beast that moos is jokingly one that makes that sound.

clue.text: Expert shipwright?

definitions.meaning: a skilled worker, a master of a trade
a craft is a vessel, so a man of craft builds ships

explanation.definitionFit: A skilled artisan is an expert; punningly, a builder of boats is a man of the craft.

clue.text: Rule 1 for a girl

parts.note: a norm is a rule or standard
A is first, as in A1

explanation.surface: A rule number one for a girl.
explanation.definitionFit: A given name: Norma is a female forename, so it stands for a girl.

clue.text: Arranged unfortunately to include one publicly accused

indicators.note: to include means the rearranged letters take in the one
unfortunately suggests things gone wrong, so the letters of arranged are disordered

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone is unluckily set up to be accused in public.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfortunately' rearranges ARRANGED into ARRAGNED, and 'to include' puts I inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To be arraigned is to be formally charged in court, publicly accused.

clue.text: He wrote about Eliza Mole

indicators.note: about signals the letters of the name are moved about

explanation.surface: A writer produced a book concerning somebody called Eliza Mole.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like 'on the subject of' but is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Emile Zola was a French novelist, a man who wrote.

clue.text: Both Dublin and Belfast opposed to peace proposal?

parts.note: Dublin is the capital of Eire
Belfast is the capital of Northern Ireland, NI
con, as in pros and cons, means against

explanation.surface: Both Irish capitals are against a proposal for peace.
explanation.walkthrough: Each city stands for its country.
explanation.definitionFit: An eirenicon is a proposal designed to make peace, from the Greek for peace.

clue.text: Workman working

definitions.meaning: a worker, especially in a factory

explanation.definitionFit: The noun means a factory hand; the adjective means in effect or functioning.

clue.text: Lebanese grower, who cared about an actor?

indicators.note: about means the letters of cared are moved about

parts.note: Herbert Beerbohm Tree was a famous English actor-manager

explanation.surface: A Lebanese farmer wonders who cared for a stage performer.
explanation.definitionFit: The cedar of Lebanon grows there and appears on the country's flag, a Lebanese plant.

clue.text: Not happy about Lawrence's place

indicators.note: about means the word for not happy goes round the initials

parts.note: not happy means sad
T.E. Lawrence, Lawrence of Arabia, gives his initials

explanation.surface: Someone is unhappy about Lawrence's home.
explanation.definitionFit: Stead means place, as in instead, in someone's place.

clue.text: Moved proposal to throw ale out

indicators.note: out means the shaken letters go outside the proposal
throw suggests tossing, so the letters of ale are jumbled

parts.note: a motion is a proposal in a debate

explanation.surface: A debate motion seeks to throw beer out of the club.
explanation.walkthrough: The jumbled ale gives EAL, split round the debating motion.
explanation.definitionFit: To be moved is to be stirred by feeling, emotional.

clue.text: It's not in a soldier to be extravagant

parts.note: something not in is out
RE, the Royal Engineers, gives a soldier

explanation.surface: An absent soldier is told to behave flamboyantly.
explanation.definitionFit: Outré, from French, means beyond the bounds, outlandish or extravagant.

clue.text: Look at letter on soil deposit

parts.note: lo is an old word for look
ess is the spelt-out name of the letter S

explanation.surface: Someone examines a letter about a soil deposit.
explanation.definitionFit: Loess is fine wind-blown silt laid down as a soil deposit.

clue.text: Metal point on supports

indicators.note: in an across clue, on means the point comes after the supports

parts.note: bras are supports
S, south, is a compass point

explanation.surface: Metal sharpened to a point sits on supports.
explanation.definitionFit: Brass is an alloy of copper and zinc, a metal.

clue.text: Reportedly be a hit man

parts.note: the cheer heard when a performance is a hit, and also an old word for a hired assassin

explanation.surface: A rumoured contract killer is on the loose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reportedly' does not mean a homophone here: it points to the shout of acclaim people report when a show is a hit.
explanation.definitionFit: The cry of acclaim for a hit is the same word as an old term for a hired killer.

clue.text: Stops at a nice part? How wicked!

indicators.note: part means only a piece of the words stops at a nice is used

explanation.surface: Someone stops at a pleasant section and finds it wicked.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'stopS AT A NICe'. 'How' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Satanic means devilish, utterly wicked.

clue.text: Avoiding girl getting ring

parts.note: Eva is a girl's name
a ding is the sound of a bell, a ring

explanation.surface: A girl dodges someone by getting a ring.
explanation.definitionFit: Evading and avoiding are synonyms for keeping away from something.

clue.text: Introducing author to a senior artificer

parts.note: leading means going first, introducing
Bram Stoker was the author of Dracula

explanation.surface: An author is introduced to a senior craftsman.
explanation.definitionFit: A leading stoker is a senior rating in a ship's engine room, a skilled hand.
